cohort: 274 placental tissues from Ivory Coastal and Ghanaian women
finding: The assessment confirmed a considerable prevalence of urogenital schistosomiasis and resistant bacterial colonization, as well as a regionally expected abundance of STI-associated pathogens.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was much more frequent in schistosomiasis patients (61.9% vs. 14.8% in women without Schistosoma spp. DNA in the placenta).
